title: Théorie des cycles algébriques : conjectures de Hodge, Tate, Lefschetz, Weil : notes manuscrites (s.d.), lettre (1965).

deep.reconstruction: Context (from p.40): A is an abelian variety over a field finitely generated over its prime field. Its Tate module T_ℓ(A) is a module over the ℓ-adic 'pseudo-algebraic' Lie algebra 𝔤, the Lie algebra of the Zariski closure of the Galois image. Base-change to K = Q̄_ℓ. Grothendieck assumes two things. (a) The Tate conjecture for divisors: H^2(A,Q_ℓ(1))^alg = H^2(A,Q_ℓ(1))^𝔤. (b) 𝔤_K acting on T_K(A) is 'pseudo-algebraic' of a very special shape: T_K(A) = V_1 ⊕ V_2, each piece an eigenspace for almost all Frobenii, with distinct eigenvalues α ≠ ᾱ on the two pieces. This page finishes the example and states the conclusion. Example: if A = C^n is a power of an elliptic curve C defined over F_q, then (a) is known (attributed to Mumford, 'au cas du produit de deux courbes elliptiques'). Condition (b) is trivial for C itself and is stable under cartesian products, so it holds for C^n. Conclusion, for all i: D^{2i}(A,Q_ℓ(i)) = H^{2i}(A,Q_ℓ(i))^alg = H^{2i}(A,Q_ℓ(i))^𝔤. Here D^{2i} (margin note) is the space of 'décomposable' Q_ℓ-algebraic classes, i.e. Q_ℓ-combinations of products of i divisor classes (modern: Lefschetz classes). Proof sketch: a priori D ⊂ alg ⊂ invariants, so it suffices that the hypotheses force the extremes to be equal. Modern verification: H^{2i}(i) = ∧^{2i}(V_1^* ⊕ V_2^*)(i) = ⊕_{a+b=2i} ∧^a V_1^* ⊗ ∧^b V_2^*. Frobenius acts on the (a,b) piece by α^{-a} ᾱ^{-b} q^i. If α/ᾱ is not a root of unity, the invariants are exactly the a=b=i piece ∧^i V_1^* ⊗ ∧^i V_2^*. This piece is spanned by products (x_1∧y_1)⋯(x_i∧y_i) of elements of V_1^*⊗V_2^* = H^2(1)^𝔤. By (a) these are divisor classes. Hence every Tate class is a product of divisor classes, and the Tate conjecture holds in all codimensions. In modern terms: the Tate conjecture for powers of a non-supersingular-type elliptic curve over a finite field follows from Tate's divisor theorem plus an invariant-theoretic computation showing that all Tate classes are Lefschetz classes.
errors: Attribution of (a) for E×E to Mumford is doubtful. Tate himself (1964–66, via Deuring) handled products of two elliptic curves, and Tate 1966 proved the divisor case for all abelian varieties over finite fields. Uncertain, possibly a slip of memory.

Hypothesis (b) requires α/ᾱ not a root of unity. It fails for supersingular curves whose Frobenius becomes scalar after extension. The conclusion still holds there (NS is maximal and all classes are Lefschetz), but not by the stated argument. The note glosses over this case.
The step from (a) to Lefschetz classes uses that the 𝔤-invariants in ∧^{2i} are generated by those in degree 2; this is only implicit ('l'hypothèse implique l'égalité des extrêmes').

ideas.what: Under the divisor Tate conjecture plus a two-eigenvalue condition on Frobenius, all Tate classes on A in every codimension are products of divisor classes. Hence the Tate conjecture holds for all i (D = alg = invariants).
ideas.modern_name: Tate classes are Lefschetz classes; Tate conjecture for products/powers of elliptic curves over finite fields
ideas.usually_credited_to: M. Spiess (Math. Ann. 1999) for products of elliptic curves over finite fields; framework of Lefschetz classes by Milne (1999), Zarhin, Murty, Tankeev

ideas.what: The chain of inclusions D^{2i} ⊂ H^{2i}_alg ⊂ H^{2i}(i)^𝔤, so equality of the extremes gives the Tate conjecture.
ideas.modern_name: Standard Lefschetz ⊂ algebraic ⊂ Tate classes sandwich

ideas.what: Using the Lie algebra 𝔤 of the Zariski closure of the Galois image, rather than the group, to compute Tate classes via invariant theory.
ideas.modern_name: ℓ-adic Lie algebra / Tate classes as 𝔤-invariants (Bogomolov, Serre)

missed.claim: Around 1965–71 Grothendieck sketches a deduction of the full Tate conjecture for powers of an elliptic curve over F_q from the divisor case. The route is an invariant-theory argument showing every Tate class is a product of divisor classes. This is essentially the argument later published by Spiess (1999), and it fits the Lefschetz-class method of Milne.
missed.quote: Alors on a partout : D^{2i}(A,Q_ℓ(i)) = H^{2i}(A,Q_ℓ(i))^{alg} = H^{2i}(A,Q_ℓ(i))^{G} ... à priori on a des inclusions ⊂, ⊂, et l'hypothèse [implique] l'égalité des extrêmes
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Historical priority: the 'Tate classes are Lefschetz' strategy for elliptic powers appears here decades before its standard published credit. The argument itself is now known.

deep.surprise_reason: A correct, early sketch of the Tate conjecture for powers of elliptic curves over finite fields via Lefschetz classes, predating Spiess/Milne. The mathematics is now standard and the case is easy once Tate's divisor theorem is known, so it is of mainly historical interest.
transcription_corrections: Margin note under D likely reads 'classes Q_ℓ-algébriques décomposables' (products of divisor classes), not 'diagonales'.
'au cas du produit de [?] {+deux+}': 'deux' is underlined; read 'au cas du produit de deux courbes elliptiques'.
'b) est trivial à partir des cas a, c' should probably read 'b) est trivial à partir du cas de C, car b) est stable par produits cartésiens'.
The exponent on the last H^{2i} is 𝔤 (the Lie algebra), not G.
'l'hypothèse indiquée[?]' is probably 'l'hypothèse implique l'égalité des extrêmes'.
'Alors on a partout' may read 'Alors on a pour tout i'.
